questions.question: Give the names and symbols of the elements with atomic numbers 1 to 10, and the symbols of sodium, potassium, iron, copper, silver, gold and lead, explaining why some symbols do not match their English names.
questions.expected_answer: 1 hydrogen H, 2 helium He, 3 lithium Li, 4 beryllium Be, 5 boron B, 6 carbon C, 7 nitrogen N, 8 oxygen O, 9 fluorine F, 10 neon Ne. Sodium Na, potassium K, iron Fe, copper Cu, silver Ag, gold Au, lead Pb. These symbols come from the Latin names of elements known since ancient times: natrium, kalium, ferrum, cuprum, argentum, aurum, plumbum.

questions.question: Define atomic number. Explain why it, and not the relative atomic mass, determines the identity and order of the elements, using argon and potassium as an example.
questions.expected_answer: The atomic number is the number of protons in the nucleus of each atom of an element. Every atom of an element has the same number of protons, and changing the number of protons changes the element (adding a proton to carbon, 6, would make nitrogen, 7), so each element has a unique atomic number from 1 to 118. Relative atomic mass does not always increase in step: argon (atomic number 18) has a relative atomic mass of 40 while potassium (19) has 39. Ordering by mass would put potassium among the noble gases; ordering by atomic number puts argon in Group 18 and potassium in Group 1 with the alkali metals, where their properties belong.

questions.question: Explain the rules for writing chemical symbols, then give the name, symbol, group and period of the elements with atomic numbers 8, 13 and 20.
questions.expected_answer: A symbol is one capital letter or a capital letter followed by one lowercase letter; the second letter is never a capital (Co is cobalt, CO is carbon monoxide, a compound). Atomic number 8: oxygen, O, Group 16, Period 2. Atomic number 13: aluminium, Al, Group 13, Period 3. Atomic number 20: calcium, Ca, Group 2, Period 4.
